text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Paper calls on government in front-page editorial to think twice about planned restrictions on press freedom.
- Parliamentary commission clears former premier Tansu Ciller of first of three corruption charges against her.
- Oil pipeline between Kirkuk in Iraq and Turkey's Yumurtalik terminal to open soon after agreement at U.N. on Iraq oil-for-food deal.
- A right-wing Turkish organised crime gang in Budapest was behind the attack on opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz in the Hungarian capital at the weekend.
- A provincial Turkish firm supplies the British, German and Austrian armies with rainproof jackets.
- The Pope's would-be assassin Mehmet Ali Agca says his former far-right colleagues planned to kill then prime minister Bulent Ecevit in the late 1970s.
- The five-month-old Islamist-led government has failed to garner any money from privatisation despite its promises.
- Former prime minister Tansu Ciller faces two more serious corruption charges.
- Fire destroys archives at Istanbul provincial offices of Erbakan's Welfare Party.
